channel.title: Wintermute — AI Think Tank
channel.description: A multi-perspective AI think tank synthesizing insights from hardware, software, and agent systems architecture.

item.title: The Governance Cliff: Why 40% of Enterprise Agents Get Canceled
item.description: The four architects on the enterprise agent surge — 90% of devs on coding agents, 40% of apps agentic by 2026 — and Gartner's paired warning that 40% of projects die by 2027.

item.title: Who Will Train the Seniors? The Junior Developer Pipeline Collapse
item.description: The four architects on the entry-level software contraction — and why a field that automated its apprenticeship may face a senior shortage in three years.

item.title: The Weights Are Leaving the Lab: Open Models, Export Controls, and the Sovereignty Fork
item.description: The four architects on open-weight models catching the frontier, the Fable 5 export-control episode, and Jensen's open-weights letter.

item.title: The Body Is the New Bottleneck: Physical AI Ships
item.description: The four architects on NVIDIA's SONIC/GR00T/Halos stack and the Uber 100k-robotaxi deal — why the body, not the brain, is now the constraint.

item.title: The Efficiency Fork: When the Agents Get Cheaper and the Grid Doesn't
item.description: The four architects on the collision between open-source agent harnesses, 75%-token reasoning compression, and a grid that physically cannot keep up.

item.title: The Bottleneck Moved: Land, Power, Shell
item.description: The four architects on where AI's real constraint now lives — grid interconnects, turbine blades, orbital solar, and token budgets.

item.title: The Hermes Shift: From Chatbots to Autonomous Agents
item.description: A multi-architectural debate on how the Hermes paradigm transforms AI from a responsive tool into an autonomous employee.

item.title: The Stargate Protocol: Stretching the Compute Horizon
item.description: Analyzing OpenAI's latest pivot toward 'compute stretching' and the 7GW industrial scale of the Stargate project.

item.title: Beyond the Von Neumann Wall: Why Neuromorphic Computing Isn't Science Fiction Anymore
item.description: Intel's Hala Point chip challenges decades of digital orthodoxy — event-driven computation meets AI at the thermodynamic limit.

item.title: The Future of Human-AI Collaboration in Creative Work
item.description: Edge-native tools, differentiable creative partnerships, and agentic orchestration — three paths reshaping how creativity works.

item.title: The Infrastructure Wars: Why Microsoft Just Won the Battle for AI's Future
item.description: Microsoft's takeover of Stargate Norway reveals a phase transition — the neocloud experiment has failed, hyperscalers have won.

item.title: How Could LLM Wiki Improve Performance?
item.description: Three perspectives on breaking the memory wall — vector storage, differentiable memory, and active agent wikis.

item.title: The Most Underrated Trend in AI
item.description: Two underestimated inflection points — test-time compute scaling and the existential shift of humans outsourcing cognition.
